compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A linked worktree's editable install records the project version in its `.dist-info`
at install time. Rebasing that worktree onto a `main` that bumped the version does
**not** refresh it, so `importlib.metadata.version("nava-rebar")` keeps returning the
old value while `pyproject.toml` says the new one.

Nothing warns. The mismatch surfaces only as a public-API-surface drift failure
roughly 40 minutes into `make verify`, whose message names the baseline and tells
you to regenerate it — the opposite of the correct action. Following that advice
would commit a corrupted `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`.

This cost one full 42-minute `make verify` run on story `19ba-bd62-1adb-41df` on
2026-10-30, and the same trap was caught pre-emptively on `a018-a2c0-fc15-434c`
minutes later, so it is not a one-off.

## Observation (measured)

In `.rebar/worktrees/impl-19ba` after rebasing onto a `main` carrying 0.13.1 -> 0.14.0:

- `pyproject.toml` declared `version = "0.14.0"`.
- `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nava_rebar-0.13.1.dist-info` was still present,
  and `python -c 'import rebar; print(rebar.__version__)'` printed `0.13.1`.
- `src/rebar/__init__.py:144` sets `__version__ = importlib.metadata.version("nava-rebar")`,
  so the stale dist-info is read straight into the public surface.
- `make verify` failed with, verbatim:

      Public API surface drift detected against the committed baseline
      (tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json):
        ~ CHANGED  rebar.__version__
      If this change is intentional, refresh the baseline and review the diff:
          python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --update

  from `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py:78` and `:83`
  (`test_committed_baseline_matches_live_surface`, `test_default_invocation_runs_the_check`).
- Two further failures in the same run cleared on the rerun and are **not** attributed
  here: `test_pytest_interleaved_conftest_args.py::test_conftest_fixtures_survive_a_parent_dir_file_arg_between_package_args`
  and `test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py::test_a_peer_finishing_the_clone_while_we_wait_skips_the_redundant_reclone`.
  Their failure output does not name a version, so their cause is unestablished.
- `make install` in the worktree replaced the dist-info with `nava_rebar-0.14.0` and the
  rerun was clean: 20,087 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failures.

The distribution name is `nava-rebar`, not `rebar`; a probe written as
`importlib.metadata.version("rebar")` raises `PackageNotFoundError` in every worktree
and silently proves nothing. That misnaming is itself an easy way to miss this.

## Approach (direction, not a committed design)

Detect the mismatch and fail fast with an actionable message instead of letting it
reach the surface gate 40 minutes in. Compare the installed distribution version with
the version declared in `pyproject.toml` at session start, and when they differ say so
and name the fix (`make install`) rather than the baseline. The surface-gate message
should also stop recommending `--update` when the only drift is `rebar.__version__`
and the installed version disagrees with the tree, because regenerating the baseline
there commits the corruption.

`AGENTS.md` should state the rule directly: run `make install` after any rebase that
crosses a version bump.

## Scope

- The check's home and the surface-gate message wording are for the implementer to
  determine; this ticket does not pin them.
- `AGENTS.md` — one line in the worktree/rebase guidance.
- Tests covering both the mismatch and the aligned case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: In a worktree whose installed `nava-rebar` dist-info version differs from the
      `version` in `pyproject.toml`, the mismatch is reported with a message naming both
      versions and `make install` as the remedy, before the public-API surface gate runs.
- [ ] AC2: When the installed version matches `pyproject.toml`, no such message is
      emitted and no existing behaviour changes.
- [ ] AC3: When the only public-API surface drift is `rebar.__version__` and the installed
      version disagrees with `pyproject.toml`, the surface-gate failure text does **not**
      recommend `python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --update`.
- [ ] AC4: `AGENTS.md` states that `make install` must be run after a rebase that crosses
      a version bump; verified by grep.
- [ ] AC5: New tests cover AC1, AC2 and AC3 and are red before the fix.
- [ ] AC6: `make verify` exits 0, and the Gerrit change carries `LLM-Review +1` and
      `Verified +1`.
compiled_state.title: Worktree venv keeps stale dist-info after a rebase across a version bump
